title: Return Values
goal: This lesson covers how to send a result back out of a function with return, so the caller can use that value.
learn: Use return to send a value back
See that return leaves the function right away
idea: return sends a value back to whoever called the function. That is different from only printing inside the function, because a returned value can be stored or used in another calculation. When Python hits return, it leaves the function immediately and hands the value back. So any lines after the return inside that function never run.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change print(double(4)) to print(double(5)) and press Run. That line of the output should say 10.

practice.text: Finish add(a, b) so it returns the sum. Print the result of calling it.
practice.hint: return sends a value back. Put the addition of a and b right after return, and do not use a print inside the function.
practice.starterTip: Change the lone return to return a + b. print(add(2, 3)) is already there; run it and you should see 5.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if add returns a + b (not only prints inside) and the sum appears in the output.

practice.text: Finish bigger(a, b) so it returns the larger of two numbers. Print two calls.
practice.hint: The if branch already returns a when a is bigger. In the else branch, return the other number.
practice.starterTip: Fill in return b in the else, then on the blank print() line try print(bigger(4, 9)) so you show two results.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if bigger returns the larger number using return and at least two call results are printed.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between print and return inside a function?

options.text: return sends the value back so it can be used; print just displays it

quiz.correct: Right, return gives the value back to your program while print only shows it.
quiz.wrong: return gives the value back to the rest of your program. print only shows it.

quiz.question: What does this print? def add(a, b): return a + b then print(add(2, 3))
quiz.correct: Yes, add returns 2 + 3, which is 5, and print shows that value.
quiz.wrong: The function returns 5 and print displays it.

quiz.question: What happens when Python hits a return line?

options.text: It pauses, then keeps running the rest of the function
It leaves the function and sends the value back
It only works inside while loops

quiz.correct: Right, return exits the function immediately with the value.
quiz.wrong: After a return, the rest of that function body does not run.

project.title: Mini Calculator Returns
project.desc: Finish four tiny functions that each take two numbers and return a result: add, subtract, multiply, and divide. Print each answer using fixed numbers, with no input().
